test_title: PYST 3: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option:

Statement 1: A surplus on the current account indicates that the country is lending to the rest of the world.

Statement 2: A current account is said to be in balance when payments exceed receipts,

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct
Neither Statement 1 nor Statement 2 is correct

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1 is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1:** A surplus on the current account indicates that the country is lending to the rest of the world. This is **correct**.

 
 
• A current account surplus occurs when a country’s total exports of goods, services, and transfers exceed its total imports.
 
• When a country exports more than it imports, it essentially generates a net financial inflow, which can be lent to other countries or invested abroad.
 
• This situation implies that the country is a net lender to the world, as it has more income than expenditure on international trade and transfers.
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** A current account is said to be in balance when payments exceed receipts. This is **incorrect**.
 
 
• A current account is considered balanced when the total receipts (income from exports, remittances, etc.) are equal to total payments (expenses on imports, transfers, etc.).
 
• If payments exceed receipts, it results in a current account deficit, not balance.
 
• Thus, the statement is factually incorrect as it misrepresents the concept of balance in the current account.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is that **only Statement 1 is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Current Account:**

 
 
• It is a component of a country’s Balance of Payments (BoP) and records the trade of goods and services, net income from abroad, and net current transfers.
 
• A positive current account balance (surplus) signifies that a country is saving more than it is investing domestically.
 
• A negative balance (deficit) indicates that a country is a net borrower from the rest of the world.
 
 
 
• **Components of Current Account:**
 
 
• **Trade Balance:** Difference between the value of exports and imports of goods and services.
 
• **Net Primary Income:** Includes income such as interest and dividends from investments abroad.
 
• **Net Transfers:** Consists of remittances, foreign aid, and other transfers between countries.
 
 
 
• **Balance of Payments (BoP):**
 
 
• The BoP is a broader measure that includes the current account, capital account, and financial account.
 
• The BoP must always balance, meaning any deficit or surplus in the current account is offset by movements in the capital and financial accounts.
 
 
 
• **Current Account Deficit (CAD):**
 
 
• Occurs when a country imports more goods, services, and capital than it exports.
 
• Financing a CAD often involves foreign borrowing or depleting foreign reserves.
 
• Persistent CAD can signal economic challenges and lead to currency depreciation.
 
 
 
• **Current Account Surplus:**
 
 
• Occurs when a country exports more than it imports.
 
• It indicates strong export performance, often associated with competitive industries and favorable trade balances.
 
• Examples of countries with consistent current account surpluses include **Germany, China, and Japan.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Current Account Balance:**

 
 
• Exchange rate fluctuations can make exports cheaper or more expensive.
 
• Economic growth and demand for imported goods.
 
• Global commodity prices, such as oil or gold.
 
• Trade policies, including tariffs and trade agreements.
 
 
 
• **Key Example:**
 
 
• India generally runs a current account deficit due to high import dependence on oil and gold.
 
• In contrast, countries like Germany and China often run current account surpluses due to strong export-driven economies.
